text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The military-dominated National Security Council refrains from a plan to reveal the minutes of a meeting connected with alleged spying as no written accord was reached on such a move.
- The Treasury aims to instill market confidence with an agreement not to seek financial resources from the central bank.
MILLIYET

- A huge project for education. Annual resources of 100 trillion lira ($629 million) will be provided to facilitate the reduction of class sizes to thirty pupils and the provision of computers in every school.
- World Bank financial assistance to Turkey, potentially as high as $5 billion in the coming three years, is largely tied to structural reform.
HURRIYET
- A mini-cabinet meeting was held by the government to discuss wide-ranging education reforms, which will in part be financed by taxes on cigarettes and alcohol.
- Islamist-led town councils will be hardest hit by Treasury plans to cut financial resources to municipalities which fail to make their foreign debt payments.
YENI YUZYIL
- Seventy-six percent of the costs of using mobile phones, now numbering over a million in Turkey, take the form of taxes.
- European Union bureaucrats are suspicious about government plans to reassess Turkey's customs union with the EU.
CUMHURIYET
- Six suspended police officers, on the run and wanted in connection with the murder of a leftist journalist, give statements after handing themselves in.
RADIKAL
- A renowned Turkish businessmen becomes only the third person in fifteen years to be awarded the state service medal for donating trillions of lira to charity.
DUNYA
- The government mulls setting up a "water bourse" to regulate the sale of excess water from southeast Turkey's huge dam and irrigation project as a potential source of funds.
ZAMAN
- Secularist plans to lengthen state education to eight years from five, seen as a threat to religious schools, are polarising society.
($1 = 159,000 Turkish lira)
